findings.evidence: Lines 54–55 introduce `[Field F]` and `[Field L]`, while `Basic.lean:73` defines `IsUnipotentPoint` for `[CommSemiring k]` and `[CommRing K]`. The action on `Comodule.groupLike ... F` is scalar multiplication by `g.ofConv x`, so its difference from identity being nilpotent makes `g.ofConv x - 1` nilpotent; `IsReduced L` suffices to make it zero.
findings.fix: Generalize the signature to `[CommSemiring F] [Semiring C] [HopfAlgebra F C] [CommRing L] [IsReduced L] [Algebra F L]`; apply the nilpotence formulation to the rank-one group-like comodule, evaluate a vanishing power at `1 ⊗ₜ 1`, and use reducedness to obtain `g.ofConv x - 1 = 0`.
findings.issue: `IsUnipotentPoint.apply_groupLike` assumes both `F` and `L` are fields, but the natural conclusion only needs a commutative semiring base and a reduced commutative target.

summary: The character theorem is unnecessarily restricted to fields even though its surrounding point API and argument naturally work over a reduced coefficient ring.
